invariants.title: Verified activation
invariants.statement: No critical system, service, policy, or governed artifact becomes active without identity, digest, compatibility, and admission verification.

invariants.title: Default deny
invariants.statement: Filesystem, network, device, process, privilege, and external-integration access is denied unless explicitly declared.

invariants.title: No implicit privilege
invariants.statement: Locality, installation, user-interface visibility, application administration, or governance influence never implies machine privilege.

invariants.title: One owner per authoritative state
invariants.statement: No component directly mutates another owner’s private authoritative state.

invariants.title: Closed privileged operations
invariants.statement: No arbitrary shell command, path, unit, device operation, or capability crosses the privileged broker.

invariants.title: Traceable active artifacts
invariants.statement: Every active governed artifact has origin, version, digest, signature policy, provenance, compatibility, and applicable SBOM evidence.

invariants.title: Accountability without indiscriminate surveillance
invariants.statement: Critical actions are traceable while event collection and disclosure remain purpose-limited and privacy-minimized.

invariants.title: Proven recovery
invariants.statement: Backup, rollback, and recovery claims require successful exercises and retained evidence.

controls.title: Current scoped threat model
controls.summary: The deployment threat model identifies protected assets, trust boundaries, adversaries, abuse cases, preventive controls, detection paths, and recovery paths for the active profile.

controls.title: Explicit control applicability by profile
controls.summary: Every active security control is classified for every profile contract as required, recommended, optional, prohibited, or not applicable.

controls.title: Control implementation validation and evidence binding
controls.summary: Every required control declares one owner, an implementation binding, a validation binding, a failure behavior, and an evidence class.

controls.title: Bounded security exceptions
controls.summary: A security exception identifies scope, owner, rationale, compensating controls, expiry, review conditions, and the conformance claims it suspends.

controls.title: Verified boot chain
controls.summary: Profiles that own the Linux boot chain verify firmware policy, bootloader, kernel, initramfs, and the selected system image before activation.
controls.applicability_condition: Not applicable when the profile does not own the host boot chain.

controls.title: Immutable verified system root
controls.summary: The active operating-system root is immutable during normal operation and verified against an admitted integrity root.

controls.title: Atomic update and last-known-good rollback
controls.summary: System and critical service updates activate atomically, preserve the prior known-good state, and never expose a partially activated release set.

controls.title: Separate verified recovery environment
controls.summary: Recovery tooling is separated from the active mutable system, independently verified, and unable to silently replace active authority.

controls.title: Hardware-rooted platform evidence by assurance level
controls.summary: Hardware-backed key protection, measured boot, and attestation are enabled only where required by the active assurance profile and remain separable from ordinary application authorization.

controls.title: Distinct human device service artifact and release identities
controls.summary: Human, device, service, artifact, release, and signing identities are distinct and cannot be substituted for one another.

controls.title: Phishing-resistant privileged and remote authentication
controls.summary: Privileged or remote administrative access uses multi-factor authentication resistant to credential replay and phishing where the profile exposes such access.

controls.title: Bounded revocable credentials
controls.summary: Credentials are scoped, expiring where practical, revocable, and invalidated when an identity, device, service, or trust relationship is retired.

controls.title: Authorization at the authoritative owner
controls.summary: A user-interface state, local network position, installed module, or successful navigation decision never substitutes for authorization by the authoritative owner.

controls.title: Default deny and least privilege
controls.summary: Filesystem, network, device, process, administrative, and cross-component privileges are denied unless explicitly declared and justified.

controls.title: Closed typed privileged broker
controls.summary: Host mutations use a narrow registered operation set with typed parameters, caller identity, policy decision, idempotence, expiry, and execution receipt.

controls.title: No arbitrary command path or unit through privilege boundary
controls.summary: The privileged boundary rejects free-form shell commands, arbitrary filesystem paths, arbitrary service names, and undeclared host operations.

controls.title: Per-service principal and bounded runtime access
controls.summary: Each service runs under a distinct principal with only its declared writable paths, sockets, devices, capabilities, and network destinations.

controls.title: Mandatory access control sandboxing and resource bounds
controls.summary: Linux profiles apply declared mandatory access control, systemd or container sandboxing, syscall restrictions where compatible, and bounded CPU, memory, process, storage, and I/O use.

controls.title: Secrets excluded from source images logs receipts and ordinary exports
controls.summary: Private keys, passwords, tokens, and equivalent secrets are not committed to source, embedded in release images, emitted in logs or receipts, or included in ordinary exports.

controls.title: Scoped offline root trust
controls.summary: Root trust is scoped by environment, release channel, artifact class, and authority domain, with the highest-impact roots retained offline.

controls.title: Key rotation revocation and compromise response
controls.summary: Every active key class has rotation, expiry, revocation, compromise declaration, replacement, and recovery procedures that are testable offline where required.

controls.title: Separated or threshold release signing by risk
controls.summary: High-impact release promotion separates build, approval, signing, and publication, and uses multiple approvals or threshold signatures where required by the active profile.

controls.title: Inbound network deny by default
controls.summary: No inbound listener is reachable beyond its declared interface, zone, identity, protocol, and profile requirement.

controls.title: Security-zone separation
controls.summary: User, application, administration, synchronization, guest, recovery, and external-integration traffic are separated where present, with interzone traffic denied unless declared.

controls.title: Declared outbound destinations for external integrations
controls.summary: External integrations use a declared gateway or egress policy with allowed destinations, data classes, quotas, timeouts, and failure behavior.

controls.title: Authenticated encrypted cross-node communication
controls.summary: Sensitive cross-node communication authenticates both endpoints and protects confidentiality, integrity, replay resistance, and protocol version negotiation.

controls.title: Data ownership classification retention and disclosure
controls.summary: Every protected data class declares one owner, sensitivity, storage boundary, access conditions, retention, disclosure, export, backup, and deletion behavior.

controls.title: Encryption and integrity for sensitive durable state
controls.summary: Sensitive durable state and its backups are encrypted at rest, and integrity-protected where unauthorized modification would affect authority or safety.

controls.title: No direct cross-owner state access
controls.summary: A component or subsystem does not directly read or write another owner’s private database, files, keys, or mutable state; declared interfaces mediate exchange.

controls.title: Quarantine for removable and offline imports
controls.summary: Untrusted removable media and offline packages are mounted without execution, copied to quarantine, and never opened directly as active authority.

controls.title: Bounded parsing signature provenance and import receipts
controls.summary: Offline admission enforces size and recursion limits, content-based type validation, signature and provenance checks, malware inspection where available, contract validation, and an immutable admission or rejection receipt.

controls.title: Pinned source dependencies and images by digest
controls.summary: Build inputs, dependencies, base images, subsystem releases, and toolchains are pinned to immutable revisions or digests and resolved without silent fallback.

controls.title: Software bill of materials for released artifacts
controls.summary: Every released OS image, service bundle, policy bundle, and applicable artifact set carries an attributable SBOM suitable for vulnerability and license review.

controls.title: Build provenance for released artifacts
controls.summary: Released artifacts carry verifiable provenance linking source, revision, builder identity, toolchain, environment, transformations, tests, and resulting digest.

controls.title: Separated build approval signing and publication
controls.summary: A single compromised build worker cannot silently produce, approve, sign, publish, and activate a high-impact release.

controls.title: Vulnerability response revocation and anti-rollback metadata
controls.summary: The release system can identify affected artifacts, revoke compromised versions or keys, publish bounded remediation, and reject stale, frozen, or unauthorized rollback metadata.

controls.title: Mandatory review static dependency and secret analysis
controls.summary: Changes to security-relevant code and configuration require review and automated analysis for code defects, vulnerable dependencies, exposed secrets, unsafe configuration, and policy drift.

controls.title: Negative testing and fuzzing of parsers and privileged protocols
controls.summary: Parsers, importers, archive handlers, protocol decoders, privileged interfaces, and security-critical state machines receive negative tests and fuzzing proportionate to risk.

controls.title: Structured security event records
controls.summary: Security-relevant events record time, event identity, actor, service, action, target, policy or decision reference, outcome, correlation, software version, and disclosure class.

controls.title: Tamper-evident bounded audit retention
controls.summary: Critical audit records are integrity-protected, append-oriented, bounded by retention policy, and independently exportable without exposing unrestricted private evidence.

controls.title: Local audit continuity during network loss
controls.summary: A network outage does not discard critical local security events; queued evidence remains bounded, inspectable, and safely transferable later.

controls.title: Privacy-minimized selective security evidence
controls.summary: Security monitoring records the minimum information required for accountability and investigation and separates public evidence from restricted proof.

controls.title: Detection alerting and containment ownership
controls.summary: Critical security signals have declared detection logic, severity, owner, containment action, escalation path, and offline behavior.

controls.title: Incident evidence preservation and coordinated response
controls.summary: Incident procedures preserve relevant evidence, protect affected people and data, coordinate key or release revocation, and record decisions, actions, and recovery authorization.

controls.title: Encrypted offline or immutable backup
controls.summary: Critical authoritative state, configuration, trust material required for recovery, and release manifests have encrypted backups with at least one offline or immutable copy.

controls.title: Regular restoration exercises
controls.summary: A backup strategy is not conforming until restoration has succeeded under the target profile with integrity, authority, and dependency checks.

controls.title: Clean-room recovery and compromise reintroduction checks
controls.summary: Recovery can occur in a clean environment and validates that restored data, configuration, keys, and artifacts do not silently reintroduce the compromise.

controls.title: Profile-specific recovery objectives and evidence
controls.summary: Each profile declares recovery point and recovery time objectives, last-known-good criteria, test frequency, and the evidence required for a recovery claim.
